soru: What are the most important works and open problems in LLM-based agents for automated software testing?

alt_sorular.soru: What are the foundations and classic (pre-LLM) methods of automated software test generation that LLM agents build upon or compare against?
alt_sorular.yeterli: Coverage is sufficient when the main classic baselines (SBST/EvoSuite, Pynguin, random testing, symbolic execution, fuzzing) and their seminal papers are identified.

alt_sorular.soru: What LLM-based methods exist for unit test generation, including prompting, iterative repair, and coverage-guided approaches?
alt_sorular.yeterli: Coverage is sufficient when the key LLM unit-test generators (TestPilot, CodaMosa, ChatUniTest, CoverUp, TestGen-LLM, HITS, etc.) and empirical evaluations of ChatGPT/Codex test generation are found.

alt_sorular.soru: How are agentic, tool-using, multi-agent LLM systems designed for software testing, such as autonomous test agents, bug reproduction, and GUI/mobile testing?
sorgular: LLM GUI testing mobile app agent
alt_sorular.yeterli: Coverage is sufficient when agent frameworks for test generation, issue/bug reproduction (LIBRO, AEGIS, Otter), and GUI/mobile testing (GPTDroid, AutoDroid, DroidAgent) are represented.

alt_sorular.soru: How are LLMs used for fuzzing and security testing, including fuzz driver generation, input generation, and protocol or compiler fuzzing?
sorgular: TitanFuzz deep learning library fuzzing LLM
alt_sorular.yeterli: Coverage is sufficient when the main LLM-fuzzing works (TitanFuzz, FuzzGPT, Fuzz4All, ChatAFL, OSS-Fuzz-Gen/fuzz driver generation) and security-testing agents are identified.

alt_sorular.soru: Which benchmarks, datasets, and evaluation metrics are used to assess LLM-based testing agents?
sorgular: mutation score coverage LLM generated tests evaluation
alt_sorular.yeterli: Coverage is sufficient when the main benchmarks (Defects4J, SWT-Bench, SWE-bench, TestGenEval, TestEval, HumanEval-derived ones) and evaluation metrics (coverage, mutation score, pass rate, flakiness) are documented.

alt_sorular.soru: Which adjacent areas reuse methods relevant to testing agents, such as test oracle generation, assertion generation, automated program repair, and software engineering agents?
alt_sorular.yeterli: Coverage is sufficient when the oracle/assertion generation (TOGA, ATLAS), mutation testing with LLMs, and SE-agent works (SWE-agent, AutoCodeRover, Agentless) that interact with testing are covered.

alt_sorular.soru: What surveys exist, and what open problems are identified, such as the oracle problem, hallucinated tests, flakiness, data contamination, cost, and industrial adoption?
sorgular: survey large language models software testing
industrial deployment LLM test generation Meta
alt_sorular.yeterli: Coverage is sufficient when the major surveys (Wang et al. 2024 TSE, Fan et al., Hou et al., LLM-agent SE surveys) and recurring open problems with supporting evidence are identified.

calismalar.baslik: Software Testing with Large Language Models: Survey, Landscape, and Vision
calismalar.gerekce: Comprehensive survey of LLMs in software testing that analyzes 102 studies and frames the field's landscape and vision.
calismalar.alinti: This paper provides a comprehensive review of the utilization of LLMs in software testing. It analyzes 102 relevant studies

calismalar.baslik: An Empirical Evaluation of Using Large Language Models for Automated Model-Based Test Generation
calismalar.gerekce: Large-scale empirical evaluation of LLMs for automated unit test generation without additional training, with repair re-prompting.
calismalar.alinti: This paper presents a large-scale empirical evaluation on the effectiveness of LLMs for automated unit test generation without additional training or manual effort

calismalar.baslik: CodaMosa: Escaping Coverage Plateaus in Test Generation with Pre-trained Large Language Models
calismalar.gerekce: CodaMosa uses pre-trained LLMs to escape coverage plateaus in test generation, an influential hybrid of classic search-based and LLM methods.

calismalar.baslik: Large Language Models are Zero-Shot Fuzzers: Fuzzing Deep-Learning Libraries via Large Language Models
calismalar.gerekce: TitanFuzz is presented as the first approach to directly use LLMs to generate input programs for fuzzing deep-learning libraries.
calismalar.alinti: we propose TitanFuzz - the first approach to directly leveraging Large Language Models (LLMs) to generate input programs for fuzzing DL libraries

calismalar.baslik: Fuzz4All: Universal Fuzzing with Large Language Models
calismalar.gerekce: Fuzz4All is presented as the first universal fuzzer, using LLMs to target many different input languages.
calismalar.alinti: This paper presents Fuzz4All, the first fuzzer that is universal in the sense that it can target many different input languages

calismalar.baslik: Large Language Models are Few-shot Testers: Exploring LLM-based General Bug Reproduction
calismalar.gerekce: LIBRO uses LLMs to automate test generation from general bug reports, a foundational LLM bug-reproduction work.
calismalar.alinti: To automate test generation from general bug reports, we propose LIBRO, a framework that uses Large Language Models (LLMs)

calismalar.baslik: Search‐based software test data generation: a survey
calismalar.gerekce: Classic survey of metaheuristic search techniques for test data generation, the pre-LLM foundation that LLM agents compare against.
calismalar.alinti: To date, metaheuristic search techniques have been applied to automate test data generation for structural and functional testing

calismalar.baslik: Feedback-Directed Random Test Generation
calismalar.gerekce: Classic feedback-directed random test generation, a key pre-LLM baseline method family for automated unit testing.

calismalar.baslik: Evaluating and Improving ChatGPT for Unit Test Generation
calismalar.gerekce: Empirical study that evaluates and improves ChatGPT for unit test generation, highlighting the potential of LLMs in this task.
calismalar.alinti: Recent work has shown the large potential of large language models (LLMs) in unit test generation.

calismalar.baslik: Effective Test Generation Using Pre-trained Large Language Models and Mutation Testing
calismalar.gerekce: MuTAP uses mutation testing to improve the bug-revealing effectiveness of LLM-generated test cases.
calismalar.alinti: we introduce MuTAP for improving the effectiveness of test cases generated by LLMs in terms of revealing bugs by leveraging mutation testing

calismalar.baslik: Make LLM a Testing Expert: Bringing Human-like Interaction to Mobile GUI Testing via Functionality-aware Decisions
calismalar.gerekce: GPTDroid lets an LLM chat with mobile apps through GUI page information, a key LLM-driven mobile GUI testing agent.
calismalar.alinti: We propose GPTDroid, asking LLM to chat with the mobile apps by passing the GUI page information to LLM to elicit testing scripts

calismalar.baslik: SWT-Bench: Testing and Validating Real-World Bug-Fixes with Code Agents
calismalar.gerekce: SWT-Bench is a benchmark for code agents that generate tests to validate real-world bug fixes, linking repair and testing agents.
calismalar.alinti: We find that LLMs generally perform surprisingly well at generating relevant test cases, with Code Agents designed for code repair exceeding the performance

calismalar.baslik: TOGA: A Neural Method for Test Oracle Generation
calismalar.gerekce: TOGA is a neural method for test oracle generation and is central to the oracle problem that LLM testing approaches inherit.
calismalar.alinti: A test oracle, typically expressed as an condition, documents the intended behavior of a unit under a given test prefix

calismalar.baslik: Large Language Model-Based Agents for Software Engineering: A Survey
calismalar.gerekce: Comprehensive, systematic survey of LLM-based agents for software engineering, including their challenges.
calismalar.alinti: In this work, we present a comprehensive and systematic survey on LLM-based agents for SE.

calismalar.baslik: Automated Unit Test Improvement using Large Language Models at Meta
calismalar.gerekce: Meta reports what it believes is the first industrial-scale deployment of LLM-generated test improvements backed by assurances of code improvement.
calismalar.alinti: We believe this is the first report on industrial scale deployment of LLM-generated code backed by such assurances of code improvement

calismalar.baslik: ChatUniTest: A Framework for LLM-Based Test Generation
calismalar.gerekce: ChatUniTest combines adaptive focal context with a generation-validation-repair mechanism, a representative iterative LLM unit-testing framework.
calismalar.alinti: ChatUniTest incorporates an adaptive focal context mechanism to encompass valuable context in prompts and adheres to a generation-validation-repair mechanism

calismalar.baslik: Demystifying LLM-Based Software Engineering Agents
calismalar.gerekce: Compares agentless and agent-based SWE systems, whose agents use tools, run commands, and observe feedback, informing testing-agent design.
calismalar.alinti: These agents are equipped with the ability to use tools, run commands, observe feedback from the environment, and plan for future actions.

calismalar.baslik: Large Language Models for Software Engineering: Survey and Open Problems
calismalar.gerekce: Widely cited survey of LLMs for software engineering that identifies open problems and stresses hybrid traditional-SE-plus-LLM techniques.
calismalar.alinti: Our survey reveals the pivotal role that hybrid techniques (traditional SE plus LLMs) have to play

calismalar.baslik: Prompt Fuzzing for Fuzz Driver Generation
calismalar.gerekce: PromptFuzz is a coverage-guided prompt fuzzer that iteratively generates fuzz drivers to explore undiscovered library code.
calismalar.alinti: we propose PromptFuzz, a coverage-guided fuzzer for prompt fuzzing that iteratively generates fuzz drivers to explore undiscovered library code

calismalar.baslik: WhiteFox: White-Box Compiler Fuzzing Empowered by Large Language Models
calismalar.gerekce: WhiteFox uses a multi-agent LLM framework in which an analysis agent examines optimization source code for white-box compiler fuzzing.
calismalar.alinti: WhiteFox adopts a multi-agent framework: an LLM-based analysis agent examines the low-level optimization source code and

calismalar.baslik: TOGLL: Correct and Strong Test Oracle Generation with LLMs
calismalar.gerekce: TOGLL presents the first comprehensive study of LLMs generating correct, diverse, and strong test oracles.
calismalar.alinti: we present the first comprehensive study to investigate the capabilities of LLMs in generating correct, diverse, and strong test oracles

calismalar.baslik: Design choices made by LLM-based test generators prevent them from finding bugs
calismalar.gerekce: Shows that LLM test-generator designs can validate bugs and reject bug-revealing tests, a key open problem.
calismalar.alinti: more alarmingly, how their design can worsen the situation by validating bugs in the generated test suite and rejecting bug-revealing tests.

calismalar.baslik: TESTEVAL: Benchmarking Large Language Models for Test Case Generation
calismalar.gerekce: TESTEVAL benchmark finds that covering specific lines, branches, or paths remains challenging for current LLMs.
calismalar.alinti: We find that generating test cases to cover specific program lines/branches/paths is still challenging for current LLMs

calismalar.baslik: Defects4J: a database of existing faults to enable controlled testing studies for Java programs
calismalar.gerekce: Defects4J is a classic, highly cited database of real Java faults that underpins controlled testing studies.

calismalar.baslik: Are Large Language Models Memorizing Bug Benchmarks?
calismalar.gerekce: Examines whether LLMs memorize bug benchmarks, addressing the data-leakage risk to valid evaluation.
calismalar.alinti: a growing concern within the software engineering community is that these benchmarks may not reliably reflect true LLM performance due to the risk of data leakage.

calismalar.baslik: Test Wars: A Comparative Study of SBST, Symbolic Execution, and LLM-Based Approaches to Unit Test Generation
calismalar.gerekce: Compares SBST, symbolic execution, and LLM-based unit test generation, finding LLMs still fall behind traditional methods in coverage.
calismalar.alinti: Our results show that while LLM-based test generation is promising, it falls behind traditional methods in terms of coverage

calismalar.baslik: Large Language Model guided Protocol Fuzzing
calismalar.gerekce: Highly cited work on LLM-guided protocol fuzzing, representing the protocol-fuzzing branch of LLM security testing.

calismalar.baslik: On the Flakiness of LLM-Generated Tests for Industrial and Open-Source Database Management Systems
calismalar.gerekce: Studies the flakiness of LLM-generated tests for industrial and open-source DBMSs, a recognized open problem.
calismalar.alinti: Recent work on LLM-based test generation has identified flakiness as a potential problem with generated tests.

calismalar.baslik: TestART: Improving LLM-based Unit Testing via Co-evolution of Automated Generation and Repair Iteration
calismalar.gerekce: TestART co-evolves automated generation and repair iteration to improve LLM-based unit testing.
calismalar.alinti: TestART improves LLM-based unit testing via co-evolution of automated generation and repair iteration, representing a significant advancement in automated unit test generation

calismalar.baslik: Towards Reliable LLM-Driven Fuzz Testing: Vision and Road Ahead
calismalar.gerekce: Vision paper identifying reliability challenges in LLM-driven fuzzing, such as low driver validity and seed quality trade-offs, that hinder adoption.
calismalar.alinti: current LLM4Fuzz solutions face critical reliability challenges, including low driver validity rates and seed quality trade-offs, hindering their practical adoption.
